title: Diary of a Madman
headline: The drummer pictured inside this Ozzy album never played on it. He'll tell you himself.
caption:
Diary of a Madman came out 45 years ago today, and the sleeve didn't tell the whole story.

The rhythm section wasn't the only mix-up. Don Airey is credited on keyboards, but he was on tour with Rainbow at the time. The parts were actually played by Johnny Cook, who'd worked with Bob Daisley in Mungo Jerry.

It was also the last Ozzy studio album with guitarist Randy Rhoads, who died in a plane crash in Florida in March 1982, during the tour for this record. Canadian journalist Martin Popoff called it "a lasting classic that stands as the definitive showcase for Randy Rhoads."

Should a reissue ever be allowed to replace the players who actually made the record?
